transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what brought you in to see me?

Ever since they made me the acting workflow lead, I’ve been stressed going into the warehouse. I’m tense before I even get there, and I’ve been snapping at little things, like SAP errors. I’m also missing cycle-count deadlines I normally wouldn’t miss. By the time I get home, I’m too drained to play basketball or work on my sketches.
When exactly did you become the acting workflow lead, and how long after that did you start noticing this tension, irritability, and difficulty meeting deadlines?
It started after the team merger. Within the first month or two, I could tell I wasn’t handling work the way I normally do.
Aside from how you feel about work, have you been feeling down, sad, or uninterested in things you normally enjoy, even on days off or in situations unrelated to your job?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed that being a separate thing from the work stress.
Besides the irritability and tension you mentioned, have you been feeling especially nervous, worried, or on edge lately, even about things unrelated to work?
I haven’t really noticed that outside of work. It mostly comes up when I’m thinking about going in or dealing with things there.
When you're dealing with this stress about work, do you notice feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or being close to tears?
I’m not sure I’d call it sadness or hopelessness. It’s more that work feels overwhelming sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed being close to tears.
Even apart from work stress, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like basketball or sketching, or is it mainly that you feel too drained to do them?

It’s mainly that work has kind of taken over. I’ve stopped going to basketball and I haven’t been doing my usual sketching time. My supervisor also had to bring up that I was missing cycle-count deadlines, so it’s affecting things at work too.
When you feel tense or on edge about work, do you also notice physical signs like your heart racing, muscle tension, or restlessness?
I’m not really sure. I just know I feel wound up when I’m thinking about work.
When you're away from work, do you find yourself worrying or ruminating about work-related problems in a way that feels hard to stop or control?
I’m not sure. I know work’s been on my mind a lot, but I don’t really know if I’d say it’s hard to control.
Over the past couple of months, have you noticed your mood being low or down most of the day, nearly every day, even during times when you're not thinking about work?
I’m not sure I’d say I’ve felt down most of the day, nearly every day. It’s more that work has been taking up a lot of space in my head.
Besides feeling overwhelmed by work, do you also notice yourself feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge in situations that have nothing to do with work?
I don’t think so. It seems mostly tied to work and everything going on there.

When you think about the work situation, would you describe your main emotional reaction as anxious or worried, or is it more a general sense of being overwhelmed and stressed without that specific anxious, on-edge feeling?
It’s more that I feel tense and overwhelmed. Since they made me acting workflow lead, I’m already wound up walking into the warehouse, and little things like SAP errors set me off.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, such as trouble falling asleep or waking up early, or changes in your appetite over the past couple of months?
I haven’t really noticed any big changes with sleep or appetite.
Besides feeling tense and irritable, have you noticed yourself acting out at work or elsewhere—like getting into arguments, breaking rules, or doing things that are out of character for you?
No, I haven’t really acted out like that. I get irritated, but I haven’t gotten into arguments or done anything out of character.
